title: Hidden Fortress
statementMd:
**This is an interactive problem!**

As part of your contribution in the Great Bubble War, you have been tasked with finding the newly built enemy fortress. The world you live in is a giant 109×109 grid, with squares having both coordinates between 1 and 109.

You know that the enemy base has the shape of a rectangle, with the sides parallel to the sides of the grid. The people of your world are extremely scared of being at the edge of the world, so you know that the base doesn't contain any of the squares on the edges of the grid (the x or y coordinate being 1 or 109).

To help you locate the base, you have been given a device that you can place in any square of the grid, and it will tell you the manhattan distance to the closest square of the base. The manhattan distance from square (a,b) to square (p,q) is calculated as |a−p|+|b−q|. If you try to place the device inside the enemy base, you will be captured by the enemy. Because of this, **you need to make sure to never place the device inside the enemy base**.

Unfortunately, the device is powered by a battery and you can't recharge it. This means that you can use the device at most 40 times.

## Input

The input contains the answers to your queries.

## Interaction

Your code is allowed to place the device on any square in the grid by writing "? i j" (1≤i,j≤109). In return, it will recieve the manhattan distance to the closest square of the enemy base from square (i,j) or −1 if the square you placed the device on is inside the enemy base or outside the grid.

If you recieve −1 instead of a positive number, exit immidiately and you will see the `wrong answer` verdict. Otherwise, you can get an arbitrary verdict because your solution will continue to read from a closed stream.

Your solution should use no more than 40 queries.

Once you are sure where the enemy base is located, you should print "! x y p q" (1≤x≤p≤109,1≤y≤q≤109), where (x,y) is the square inside the enemy base with the smallest x and y coordinates, and (p,q) is the square inside the enemy base with the largest x and y coordinates. **Note that answering doesn't count as one of the 40 queries.**

After printing a query or printing the answer, do not forget to output end of line and flush the output. Otherwise, you will get `idleness limit exceeded`. To do this, use:

- `fflush(stdout)` or `cout.flush()` in C++;
- `System.out.flush()` in Java;
- `flush(output)` in Pascal;
- `stdout.flush()` in Python;
- See the documentation for other languages.
statementZhMd:
**这是一道交互题！**

作为伟大泡泡战争中的一员，你的任务是寻找新建成的敌方堡垒。你所生活的世界是一个巨大的 109×109 网格，其中每个方格的两个坐标都在 1 到 109 之间。

你知道敌方基地是一个矩形，其边与网格的边平行。这个世界的人们非常害怕待在世界的边缘，因此你知道基地不包含网格边缘上的任何方格（即横坐标或纵坐标为 1 或 109 的方格）。

为了帮助你定位基地，你获得了一个设备，可以将其放置在网格中的任意方格内。设备会告诉你该方格到基地中最近方格的曼哈顿距离。方格 $(a,b)$ 到方格 $(p,q)$ 的曼哈顿距离为 |a−p|+|b−q|。如果你尝试将设备放置在敌方基地内部，就会被敌人俘获。因此，**你必须确保设备从不被放置在敌方基地内部**。

遗憾的是，该设备由电池供电，且无法充电。这意味着你最多只能使用设备 40 次。

## 输入格式

输入包含对查询的回答。

## 交互

你的程序可以通过输出 `? i j` 将设备放置在网格中的任意方格上（1≤i,j≤109）。作为回应，你将获得从方格 (i,j) 到敌方基地中最近方格的曼哈顿距离；如果你放置设备的方格位于敌方基地内部或网格外，则返回 −1。

如果收到的不是正数而是 −1，请立即退出，此时你将得到 `wrong answer` 判定。否则，由于你的程序会继续从已关闭的输入流中读取内容，你可能会得到任意判定。

你的程序使用的查询次数不得超过 40 次。

当你确定敌方基地的位置后，应输出 `! x y p q`（1≤x≤p≤109,1≤y≤q≤109），其中 (x,y) 是敌方基地内部横坐标和纵坐标均最小的方格，(p,q) 是敌方基地内部横坐标和纵坐标均最大的方格。**注意，输出答案不计入 40 次查询。**

输出查询或答案后，别忘了输出换行并刷新输出缓冲区。否则，你将得到 `idleness limit exceeded`。具体来说，可以使用：

- C++ 中的 `fflush(stdout)` 或 `cout.flush()`；
- Java 中的 `System.out.flush()`；
- Pascal 中的 `flush(output)`；
- Python 中的 `stdout.flush()`；
- 其他语言请参阅相应文档。
